source.title: Armagh Guardian, 1 May 1908, p. 3 ("For Armagh Rural Council": nominations; "a" = against direct labour, "d l" = direct labour)
source.publisher: Armagh Guardian (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name read from the page image; "no contest", no poll

note: Triennial election of the rural district council, polled 27 May 1908; "there were only six contests". Ballyards (Andrew Davidson, George Brown, Thomas Quinn, senr., nominated) is not in the results; the Irish News says the Nationalists gained a seat there, but the members returned were not found, so it is not filed. The nomination list marks candidates "a" (against direct labour) or "d l" (direct labour); these are not party labels and are not filed as such. Returned unopposed. James Irwin: no party label printed in 1908. At other elections he stood as Unionist (East Ward, Armagh Urban District, 16 January 1905, printed 'Unionists': Armagh Guardian, 13 January 1905, p. 5 ("Armagh municipal elections: withdrawals in two wards"); St. Mark's Ward, Armagh Urban District, 15 January 1908, printed 'Unionists': Northern Whig (weekly), 11 January 1908, p. 5 ("Urban council elections"); East Ward, Armagh Urban District, 16 January 1911, printed 'Unionists': Armagh Guardian, 20 January 1911, p. 3 ("Municipal elections: Nationalists retain majority in Armagh")).
